note.purpose: The line under a step caption, in Soft Ink.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing in the build: step feed, stamp drop and button color swaps.

motion.name: feed
motion.value: 560ms ease-out; clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) to inset(0), translateY(-8px) to 0
motion.purpose: Each step of the slip fills in from above, in order.

motion.name: stamp
motion.value: 300ms ease-out; opacity 0 to 0.94, rotate(-6deg) scale(1.5) to scale(1)
motion.purpose: The stamp comes down once, after the last step; it then stays set.

motion.name: swap
motion.purpose: Button hover. Removed under prefers-reduced-motion, as are feed and stamp.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Head, slip and form lines go to one column; perforation turns horizontal; stamp moves onto the rows.

breakpoints.name: nav-scroll
breakpoints.purpose: Top nav becomes one scrolling row.

narrative.overview:
Every answer is a cheque with its carbon copy. The original slip, on pale cheque paper over a fine guilloche security pattern, carries what the visitor asked, the form the AI filled in, the check, the SQL and the rows. The carbon copy, torn off down a line of punched holes and printed in indigo, carries only what the AI was shown: table and column names over empty cells, and the count of rows sent to it, always zero. A red rubber stamp lands on the result. The page is a business document, not an app screen: hard ink rules, square corners, no shadows, no cards floating on a canvas.

Rank comes from one variable grotesk pushed through weight, width and case, not from a second family or a parade of sizes. Color is semantic before it is decorative: indigo means "the AI saw this", red means "audited, refused, hidden or measured", blue means "a line you write on". Depth is the change of paper (sage page, near-white slip, lavender-grey carbon) and the weight of the rule between them.

Scope: the front page (`/`) and the ask flow (`/try/`) are built in this world and share `web/src/tokens.css`. Results (`/results/`) and Value (`/value/`) still load the older `style.css` and are not yet in this world; they are not described here and are not a source for new work.
keyCharacteristics: Sage cheque paper with a guilloche security pattern, densest on the slip, faint on the page head, never behind long-read paragraphs.
One family, Archivo variable, ranked by weight (400 to 880), width (78% to 115%) and uppercase tracking.
2px ink frames, 1px subdivisions, square corners everywhere.
Indigo carbon reserved for what the AI was shown; absence drawn as empty dashed cells.
A red rotated rubber stamp with uneven ink as the single mark of a checked result.
Flat: no box shadows, no gradients, no glow.

rules.name: The Carbon Rule
rules.body: Indigo on carbon paper means "this is what the AI was shown". Nothing the AI did not see is printed in carbon.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Red audits, blue lines the form, indigo is the carbon. A color that carries no one of those meanings stays ink.

rules.name: The Weight-and-Width Rule
rules.body: Rank is set by weight, width and case within one family. Don't add a second display face or a new size where a weight or width step does the job.

rules.name: The Caption Rule
rules.body: Uppercase labels caption a field, a step, a table column or a block of the slip, as printed captions do on a cheque. They never sit above a headline as a kicker.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never lift. If something needs separating, change the paper or draw a rule.

dos: Do take every color from `tokens.css`; Ink, Slip White and the three working inks cover the build.
Do print anything the model receives on carbon paper in indigo, and nothing else.
Do draw absence: an empty dashed cell, a struck-through hidden column, "Rows sent to the AI: 0".
Do separate with rules: 2px ink for frames and table heads, 1px for rows and steps, red rules for ledgers of audited facts, blue rules for lines you write on.
Do set numbers in tables and outputs with tabular figures and a slashed zero.
Do keep the guilloche off long-read copy; it belongs on the page head and the slip.
donts: Don't round a corner or add a box shadow, gradient or glow.
Don't add a second type family for display; reach for Archivo's weight and width instead.
Don't use the red stamp for anything but the checked or refused result.
Don't put an uppercase label above a headline as a kicker; labels caption fields, steps and tables.
Don't build the AI-landing layout of a headline beside a chat screenshot or a row of feature cards.
